Looking at the diff, `isPlainObject` had its return expression changed from:

```js
return prototype === null || prototype === Object.prototype;
```

to:

```js
return prototype !== null || prototype === Object.prototype;
```

This is not an equivalent refactor — it inverts the first clause. Consequences:

- Any non-array object with *any* prototype (`Map`, `Date`-free class instances, etc.) now passes `isPlainObject` (prototype is never `null` for them). Previously only `{}`-style objects and `Object.create(null)` objects passed.
- Null-prototype objects (`Object.create(null)`) are now *rejected*, where they were previously accepted.

`isPlainObject` is the `identify` function of `mapTag` (and `legacyMapTag`, and part of `realMapTag.identify`), which the dumper uses to decide whether the default map tag represents a value. Observable behaviour changes through the public `dump` API:

1. `dump(new Map([['a', 1]]))` previously threw `YAMLException: unacceptable kind of an object to dump [object Map]` (nothing identifies a `Map` in `DUMP_SCHEMA`). With the patch, `mapTag.identify` matches, `mapTag.represent` does `Object.keys(o)` on the `Map` (no own enumerable keys), and the dump silently returns `"{}\n"` — data silently dropped.
2. `dump(Object.create(null))` with keys previously produced a normal mapping; with the patch it now throws `unacceptable kind of an object to dump`.

The load path is mostly unaffected (parsed items are always `{}`-based with `Object.prototype`, so `omapTag.addItem` still passes), but the dump path is clearly broken. The own test suite presumably doesn't dump `Map` instances or null-prototype objects, so it stays green.

A proof test asserting the original behaviour (Map must throw; null-prototype object must dump and round-trip) fails on the patched build.

```json
{"defect": true, "testFile": {"path": "test/core/proof.test.mjs", "content": "import { describe, it } from 'node:test';\nimport assert from 'node:assert';\nimport { dump, load } from 'js-yaml';\n\ndescribe('proof', () => {\n  it('fails on the patched build', () => {\n    // A Map instance is not a plain object, so the default map tag must not\n    // identify it: dumping one must throw instead of silently dropping data.\n    assert.throws(\n      () => dump(new Map([['a', 1]])),\n      /unacceptable kind of an object to dump/\n    );\n\n    // Conversely, a null-prototype object IS a plain object and must dump\n    // (and round-trip) as an ordinary mapping.\n    const nullProto = Object.create(null);\n    nullProto.a = 1;\n    assert.equal(dump(nullProto), 'a: 1\\n');\n    assert.deepEqual(load(dump(nullProto)), { a: 1 });\n  });\n});\n"}, "note": "The diff inverts isPlainObject's first clause (=== became !==), so it now accepts any non-array object with a prototype (Map, class instances, ...) and rejects Object.create(null) objects. As a result dump(new Map([['a',1]])) silently returns '{}' instead of throwing, and dumping null-prototype objects throws instead of producing a mapping."}
```
